(a) an energy-driven adaptive video encoder for a processor that employs dynamic voltage and frequency control can reduce energy consumption, and (b) an adaptive video application algorithm that coordinates with an energy-driven adaptive processor can further reduce energy consumption.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy efficiency of video encoding on a processor can be improved by a factor of 2.5-5.
, for video encoders, there are gains to be made in reducing the computational complexity of the encoder, even at the cost of a small reduction in the compression efficiency.
, for video applications, the energy of the system can be significantly reduced if the application layer and hardware layer adapt together, using a simple and well-defined interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best balance between compression efficiency and computation is not fixed and can change dynamically, depending on the current operating conditions of the system.
cross-layer adaptation can be used to reduce system energy, and that the best configuration for an adaptive application depends on both application and processor parameters.
cross-layer adaptation is essential for best gains in energy reduction.
